Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corporation Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; Tom Reilly, Chief Operating Officer; and Mike Harlan, VP of Exploration.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy delivered solid results in Q3 2024, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved average production of 450,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, alongside meaningful progress in our ESG initiatives, including an 18% year-over-year reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on operating expenses per BOE, which fell to $8.42. We are focused on advancing our exploration and drilling activities, highlighted by standout well results in the Permian. Further, we are working on midstream infrastructure developments to support transportation volumes. Finally, we are taking steps to refine our production guidance for the coming periods, positioning us for sustained growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Elena. As Elena mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $2.8 billion, up 25% year-over-year. Operating income was $850 million, and net income was $620 million. We generated $1.1 billion in free cash flow and returned $450 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $5.2 billion in debt and $2.3 billion in cash.

Before moving to operational updates, let me dive deeper into our operating expenses per barrel of oil equivalent, or OpEx per BOE, which has been central to our cost leadership strategy and enables robust free cash flow generation even at moderate WTI prices around $65 to $70. In Q3 2024, consolidated OpEx per BOE landed at $8.42, marking a 12% sequential improvement from Q2's $9.55 and an 18% decline from Q3 2023's $10.28. This positions us at the low end of our full-year guidance midpoint of $8.50 to $9.00 per BOE, and looking back, we've reduced costs by nearly 30% from the 2021 peak of $12.10 per BOE, which was pressured by pandemic supply chain issues, labor constraints, and elevated workover expenses.

The trajectory shows clear progress: 2021 averaged $12.10 per BOE with lease operating expenses at $7.20 amid high chemical and field service costs; 2022 improved 14% to $10.45 through Permian scale-up and inflation hedging; 2023 dropped another 12% to $9.15 as deflation set in post-energy shocks, with gathering, processing, and transportation costs falling 20% to $2.10; and now Q3 2024 at $8.42, broken down to LOE of $4.85 down 15% year-over-year, GPT at $1.95 down 22% from optimized contracts, and G&A at $1.62 flat on a per-BOE basis. This reflects disciplined execution across our 450,000 net BOE per day base, 70% oil-weighted, primarily from Permian Delaware Basin at 65%, Eagle Ford at 20%, and Bakken at 15%.

In the Permian, OpEx hit $6.80 per BOE, rivaling Pioneer and Occidental's sub-$7 figures, thanks to scale from over 1,200 horizontal Delaware wells with 12,500-foot average laterals and advanced 3D seismic to limit interference. Eagle Ford rose slightly to $9.20 due to water disposal pressures from regulatory limits, but recycled water now covers 45% of usage, up from 25%. Bakken at $11.50 reflects pipeline tolls and winterization but improved 10% via ESP run-life extensions to 650 days.

Our strategies span optimization, digitalization, and portfolio discipline. Operationally, we've cut LOE through optimized chemicals with Halliburton and SLB, down 25% to $0.45 per BOE, ceramic proppants in 30% of Permian fracs saving 18% on transport, VSD upgrades on 40% of 2,500 ESPs boosting efficiency to 96% and trimming $0.30 per BOE, and AquaCycle water recycling at 50% in Eagle Ford avoiding $1.50 disposal fees. GPT savings came from renegotiating 60% of contracts with Targa and Energy Transfer into 15-year take-or-pays 10% below prior rates, saving $0.45 per BOE against Waha basis volatility.

Digitally, our $75 million Apex Digital platform delivers 4x ROI: AI predictive maintenance via AspenTech reduces downtime 28% in Bakken, drones and IoT cover 80% of 5,000-mile gathering saving 35% on labor, and digital twins optimize Delaware pads for 15% IP30 uplift deferring $0.20 per BOE. Portfolio moves include divesting $200 million non-core Bakken at high OpEx, Permian bolt-ons, D&C at $650 per foot versus industry $750, and diesel hedges at $2.40 per gallon.

This fortifies our balance sheet with $450 million levered FCF at $70 WTI, 20% IRRs at $55 oil, and a recent $1.2 billion Permian acquisition at sub-$8 per BOE multiples. Risks like 5% labor inflation or EPA rules add $0.30 potential, but hedging and automation keep us flat-to-down for the year, backing $1.8 billion FCF and 15% dividend growth.

Shifting to our midstream segment, which provides stable fee-based revenues making up about 45% of adjusted EBITDA at $450 million this quarter, up 12% year-over-year. Transportation volumes grew robustly: crude throughput averaged 1.85 million barrels per day on Permian Gateway and Longhorn, up 15% YoY and 8% sequentially at 92% utilization, with Permian output at 6.5 million barrels daily narrowing Waha basis to -$0.25 per barrel, yielding $0.85 tariff revenue under 95% take-or-pay coverage. Natural gas hit 7.2 Bcf per day on Northern Access and Southern Lights, up 18% YoY from Haynesville ramps for LNG, processing 2.1 Bcf per day into 145,000 barrels per day NGLs at Mont Belvieu's 320,000 barrels per day fractionation amid firm petchem demand. Products pipelines moved 450,000 barrels per day, up 10% YoY post-TMX. Permian drove 65% of volumes, Appalachia and Haynesville 25% growth, offset by minor hurricane downtime recouped via credits.

Infrastructure capex of $1.2 billion is 5% ahead, targeting 15-18% yields: Permian Highway 2.0 JV with Enterprise adds 200,000 barrels per day to Gulf Coast, in-service September at 98% utilization with $120 million annual EBITDA from Oxy and Pioneer contracts; Haynesville Connector Phase II loops 120 miles to 2.5 Bcf per day feeding Plaquemines LNG with advanced leak detection cutting O&M 15%; Nederland storage adds 2 million barrels leased to traders, NGL splitter boosts recoveries 8,000 barrels per day for $25 million 2025 EBITDA.

We're capitalizing on Permian buildouts and LNG doubling to 20 Bcf per day by 2026, with 70% 2025 volumes hedged, 25% capex on emissions cuts via electrification and CCUS pilots. Full-year midstream EBITDA guides $1.85 to $1.95 billion, 14% growth, Q4 up 10% QoQ at 93-95% utilization for 8-10% distribution growth, backed by 85% contracted backlog despite some regulatory reviews.

I will now turn the call over to Tom Reilly for an operational update.

Tom Reilly: Thank you, Sarah. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 450,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought the Blackhawk 12H-4 well online, which is expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives.

Now I will turn it over to Mike Harlan for an update on our exploration activities.

Mike Harlan: Thank you, Tom. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Permian Basin and are planning to drill 160 exploration wells in the next year. We believe these wells have the potential to add significant reserves to our portfolio.

Our strategy centers on high-return basins like the Permian and emerging Gulf of Mexico plays. In 2024 so far, we've drilled 142 gross operated wells, up 18%, within $1.2 billion D&C capex at 65% of upstream spend. Permian dominated with 112 spuds across 145,000 net acres at 98% success: Blackhawk 12H-4 in Reeves County Delaware hit 11,850 feet TD, 3-mile lateral, 2,450 BOE/d IP30 (68% oil), 1.8 MMboe EUR, sub-$35 breakeven via Super Frac with 65 stages, 4,500 lbs/ft proppant; replicated on 10-well pad at 2,100 average IPs, growing inventory to 1,200 locations at 10% IRRs. Midland's Mustang 78H-2 posted 1,950 BOE/d IP45 (72% oil), 1.5 MMboe EUR, costs down 12% to $650/ft with Nabors automated rigs cutting cycle times 2.5 days. Permian output reached 185,000 BOE/d, up 25% QoQ, targeting 210,000 year-end at low-$30s breakevens.

Eagle Ford's 18 wells on 80,000 acres, like Rio Bravo 15H pad at 1,800 BOE/d IP30 (45% liquids), 1.2 MMboe EUR, 85% cluster efficiency via diverters, extending runway to 350 locations. Gulf of Mexico's Blacktip prospect (25% WI) discovered 120 feet pay, 8,500 bbl/d + 25 MMcf/d DST, 15-20 MMboe potential de-risking 50 wells; $150 million for two 2024 developments. Guyana Stabroek appraisal confirms pay akin to Liza.

Technically, SLB Delfi and AI optimize bits/muds to <3% NPT, CubeFrac stacks benches for 20% EUR gains, 95% gas capture cuts emissions 28%. 2024 plan: 160 wells (120 Permian, 25 Eagle Ford, 15 GoM/Guyana), 12-14 rigs, $1.4 billion capex, 20,000 Permian acres bolt-on, EOR pilots ahead. This drives 15-20% growth, 12% FCF yields at $50 WTI.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Energy Capital Partners. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks, and good morning, team. Could you walk us through the progress on your ESG initiatives, particularly emissions reduction targets? We've seen some peers like ExxonMobil and Chevron pushing hard on methane pledges—how are you stacking up?

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Good morning, Sarah. Great question, and one we're hearing frequently as investors prioritize the energy transition. I'll turn this over to Mike Harlan, our VP of Exploration, who's also leading key aspects of our ESG strategy.

Mike Harlan: Thanks, Elena, and good morning, Sarah. Our ESG framework rests on three pillars: environmental stewardship, social responsibility, and governance excellence, with emissions reduction at the core of our environmental efforts. We're committed to the Science Based Targets initiative and Oil and Gas Climate Initiative, aiming for net-zero Scope 1 and 2 by 2050 with stringent interim goals.

In Q3 2024, we reduced absolute Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions 18% year-over-year to 22.4 million metric tons CO2e from 27.3 million, surpassing our 2025 target of 25 million tons. Flaring dropped 12% to 0.8% of gross gas, below our 1% goal and World Bank 2030 zero routine target. Methane intensity improved 25% to 0.22% of marketed gas, beating 0.30% 2025 target early and ranking top quartile versus ConocoPhillips' 0.25%. Upstream flaring intensity fell to 0.45% from 1.2% in 2022 via Permian gas capture.

In U.S. Permian (450,000 net BOE/d), 65% rig/fract fleet electrification via grid and solar cut diesel 28% or 150,000 gallons daily, tied to $500 million ApexNet JV with Kinder Morgan capturing 95% gas, down 22% emissions. Offshore Guyana Stabroek (1.2 million BOE/d gross) uses subsea tiebacks and FPSO pilots, cutting vented emissions 35%; Yellowtail first oil H1 2025 with CCUS prep alongside Exxon/Hess. North Sea Buzzard redevelopment adds VRUs, reducing methane 40% ahead of UK mandates amid $90/ton taxes. UAE ADNOC JV scales CCUS to 1.2 million tons captured yearly via Habshan, our 300,000-ton share aiding EOR by 10-15% and offsetting 15% emissions with Shell tech.

We've deployed continuous monitoring with drone OGI, GHGSat LDAR on 80% assets detecting 1 kg/hr leaks, and ApexPredict AI preempting 92% issues, cutting repairs 30%. CCUS advances include $1.2 billion Texas hub with Occidental for 5 mtpa by 2028 under 45Q, and Climeworks DAC pilots.

This drives value: 'A' CDP rating, S&P ESG Index, $2.5 billion green bonds at 75 bps savings. Amid EU CBAM and U.S. $900/ton methane fees, our $20-40/ton abatement costs beat industry $50-80, derisking $15 billion capex versus BP's cuts. Challenges include offshore grid limits and 450 million-ton Scope 3; we're advancing OGCI low-carbon LNG like Qatar North Field blue hydrogen.

Q3 keeps us ahead: 15% full-year Scope 1+2 cut, methane <0.25%, flaring <1%, generating long-term alpha. Happy for follow-ups.

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Thanks, Mike. That highlights our transition readiness alongside 12% upstream returns.

Operator: Our next question comes from John Doe with XYZ Capital. Please go ahead.

John Doe: Good morning. Could you provide more detail on production guidance for next quarter and the full year, including key factors influencing those projections?

Sarah Jenkins: Great question, John, and thanks for joining. Production outlook is key to our disciplined framework targeting 45% free cash flow yield at $75+ WTI and $3.50 Henry Hub.

For Q4 2024, we guide 248,000 to 258,000 BOE per day, up 2% from Q3's 245,000, with oil 155,000 to 165,000 barrels per day, NGLs 45,000 to 50,000, gas 290 to 310 MMcf per day at 62% oil cut from Permian sweet crude premium.

Full-year 2024 narrows to 242,000 to 252,000 BOE per day, up from prior 238,000-248,000, oil 150,000-160,000, 8% YoY growth from 2023's 225,000, ramping to 260,000-270,000 in Q4.

Drivers center on Permian (72% mix): 28 DUCs online Q4 with 12,500-foot laterals at 2,200 BOE/d IP30, 1.6 MBOE EUR/ft via 3,500 lbs/ft proppant, diverters, 18-day cycles with SLB Neuro, five frac crews at $650/ft. Eagle Ford flat-up 1% on five pads with 40 bbls/MMCF NGLs, 2 MMcf/d from midstream JV. Bakken steady, testing 1,800 BOE/d extended laterals.

$1.8 billion capex 85% D&C funds Tier 1 1,200 locations sub-$50 breakeven, methane 0.15%, 92% water recycle. Offsets: 8-12,000 BOE/d turnarounds ($45 million ESP swaps), weather with $500 million liquidity. OPEC+ and LNG support macros; at $65 WTI, defer crews for +2% hold.

This enables 10% CAGR to 2026, maximizing NPV-10 like Pioneer. Happy to follow up.

Operator: Our next question comes from Jane Smith with ABC Securities. Please go ahead.

Jane Smith: Good morning. What are your expectations for exploration and drilling activity updates, including key well results?

Mike Harlan: Thanks, Jane, and good morning. Building on my earlier remarks, our exploration and drilling are advancing strongly in inventory-rich areas. We've spudded extensively in Permian Delaware and Midland, with Blackhawk exemplifying results at exceptional IPs and EURs through enhanced frac designs and efficiencies. Eagle Ford and Gulf of Mexico/Guyana add diversity with high success rates and de-risked follow-ons. Technically, low NPT, multi-bench fracs, and ESG-integrated gas capture position us for 160 wells next year at compelling returns, supporting decade-long growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Bob Wilson with DEF Advisors. Please go ahead.

Bob Wilson: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

Mike Harlan: Excellent point, Bob. These results reinforce our focus on core Permian expansion, bolt-on acquisitions, and selective international plays, enhancing reserves and production compounding while maintaining capital discipline and low breakevens to navigate commodity cycles.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Dr. Elena Vasquez for closing remarks.

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
